summary: All fourteen findings confirmed; most fixes are amended. /1 (high): the dihedral counterexample holds — Theorems 27.1, 30.1 and 31.11 fail when Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_K∘Nrd), for fixed data at the other places; the hypothesis must also go on items /94 and /95. /2 (high): /48 drops 'k algebraically closed' and /56 drops 'O_{π,σ} non-empty'; the red team's SO(2,1) reason for /56 is wrong (a correct counterexample is U(1,1) ⊃ U(1)), but the fix is right. /3 and /12: the copied slips and the further mistakes are all real (all in arXiv v3 except /12(viii)); /12(ii) affects a stated result, /12(iii) amends E3. /5: route /30 to AF.1 (AF.1b) and the real Plancherel theorem to the AutomorphicSpectralTheory Part II; leaving it unrouted fails the checker. /6: /72 to SR.3, but Waldspurger's p-adic Plancherel formula has no other owner. /7: LP2/LP3 routes of BHKT-19 and LAFFORGUE-18 already own affine GIT; /46 says 'unstable' for 'not H-stable'. /8: GGP owns the local period; route 1 keeps the orthonormal-basis sum. /9: GN.4 with a packet request, keeping unipotent-flow ownership whole. /10: the reductive Harish-Chandra isomorphism and Chevalley restriction need one foundational owner. /4, /11, /13, /14 confirmed with corrections (uniform admissibility is planned at SR.3a; add Borel density; MAO-WAN-ZHANG-26 never had a GGP route; review blocks only on E1, E8, E9, E11, E14).

findings.reason: I read §25.1–25.7 (pp. 167–172), §26 (pp. 172–180), §27 (pp. 180–186), §28–31 (pp. 187–204) of the published text. §25.7 allows (SO_{n+1}, SO_n) with n ⩾ 2, G and H anisotropic, G_p compact at archimedean p ≠ q, G quasi-split at q, π and π′ tempered and π generic. Theorem 27.1 asserts (1/τ(H))∫_{[H]}[a] = (1/τ(G))∫_{[G]}[a] for the limit states [a] = lim h^d[Op_h(a) ⊗ T′], T′ a fixed positive tensor in π′ ⊗ π̄′ of trace 1 (§26.3; any T′ = u ⊗ ū is allowed). Lemma 27.3 reduces this to G∞⁺-invariance of [δ_ξ] (Theorem 27.7, via Ratner) plus surjectivity of H(A) → ε = G(F)G∞⁺U\G(A), which it derives place by place from surjectivity of the spinor norm on SO_{n−1} 'for n − 1 ⩾ 2'. Lemma 30.4 applies (27.1), and Theorems 30.1 and 31.11 follow from it. I checked the counterexample step by step. (a) Data. F = Q, D an indefinite quaternion division algebra, G = PD^× = SO(D⁰, Nrd), K ⊂ D imaginary quadratic, H = K^×/Q^× = SO(K^⊥ ∩ D⁰). A GGP pair: H is the stabiliser of √d ∈ K⁰, and V_H = Kj has −disc giving K. The spinor norm on PD^× is Nrd modulo squares, so χ = η_K∘Nrd. Π = JL(π(ψ)) with ψ a Hecke character of K, ψ|_{A^×} = η_K (trivial central character; such ψ exist, e.g. from CM elliptic curves), D ramified only at primes where π(ψ) is supercuspidal (these are non-split in K, so K embeds in D), and Π_∞ = D_k, which is tempered and generic, as §25.7 requires. Then Π ⊗ χ ≅ Π. (b) χ is trivial on G(F) (η_K is trivial on Q^×), on H(A) (Nrd restricted to K is the norm) and on G(A)⁺. Hence ∫_{[H]}φΣ̄ = ∫_{[H]}(χφ)Σ̄. (c) By multiplicity one for D^×, multiplication by χ is an involution M of Π that factors as ⊗M_v with M_v : Π_v → Π_v ⊗ χ_v. At ∞, M_∞ commutes with PGL₂(R)⁺ and anticommutes with diag(1, −1), which swaps D_k^±. So M_∞ = c·sgn(n) on SO(2)-weight n. H_∞ = SO(2) lies in the identity component, so the H_∞-functional (projection to weight n) is multiplied by c·sgn(n). At finite v, χ_v|_{H_v} = 1 and toric multiplicity one (Tunnell–Saito) give ℓ_v∘M_v = ±ℓ_v. At v ∉ R the sign does not depend on Σ: at split v, χ_v = 1 and M_v is a scalar; at inert v, Σ_v is trivial. (d) So, with the components σ′ at R∖{q} fixed, the global H-period of Π vanishes identically for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, and P = 0 in (25.1) gives L(Π, Σ) = 0. (e) Take the finite places of R non-split in K. Then H_p is compact, its l-components are single supercuspidal points, and these are allowable by Theorem 24.5 (§24.2). So U′ = {σ′} is admissible. Take U a nice interval on the vanishing side of [h^∧] ∩ image(O_stab) = R∖{0}; the upper and lower nilcone sheets project to the two half-lines. Then F_h is non-empty by Lemma 31.9, and every term of (31.3) is 0, so the average is 0, not 1/2. The same choice with k supported on one side and k′ = 1_{σ′} contradicts Theorem 30.1 and Corollaries 31.4/31.8. (f) For (27.1) directly: [a] is a function on the finite group ε, the image of H(A) is ker χ (index 2 once θ(U) ⊆ ker η_K), and (27.1) ⟺ ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = 0. With T′ = u ⊗ ū for u an M′-eigenvector (χ is automatically trivial on the stabiliser of u), ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = lim h·tr(M_∞Op_h(a))·⟨M′u, u⟩ = ±c(∫_{O⁺}a − ∫_{O⁻}a), which is non-zero for a supported near one sheet. The failure matches the root numbers: L(½, π_K ⊗ Ω) = L(½, ψΩ)L(½, ψ^cΩ), and with the finite data fixed, flipping the sign of the weight multiplies each archimedean root number by (−1)^{k−1} = −1 for even k. (g) (1.4) survives. [a] ⩾ 0, and ε/im H(A) injects into A^×/Q^×N(A_K^×) ≅ Z/2, using Kneser's θ(G(F)) = F^× ∩ θ(G(A)) for dim V = 3. So the left side of (27.1) is at most twice the right, and the upper-bound half of the argument gives L(Π, Σ) = o(C^{1/4}). (h) The real-place remark is also right. At a real place where V_H is definite and V is not (at q: (SO(2,1), SO(2)) and (SO(3,1), SO(3)), both quasi-split), θ(H_q) = 1 while θ(G_q) = {±1}, so the place-by-place claim is false even for n − 1 = 3. For dim V_H ⩾ 3 Kneser's theorem supplies the sign from G(F); only the proof is affected. (i) Under the hypothesis Π ≇ Π ⊗ χ, the repaired Theorem 27.1 holds: χ is the only character of ε trivial on im H(A), and ∫[a]χ = 0 because Π ⊥ Π ⊗ χ. So the corrected statements are right. The text is identical in arXiv v3 (proof of Lemma 27.3). Corrections to the fix: (1) Also add the hypothesis to item /94 (Theorem 30.1, whose note covers Lemma 30.4) and item /95 (Corollaries 31.4 and 31.8), which fail in the same example; the fix names only /85, /86, /98 and /99. (2) In the rewritten E1, the one-sided vanishing is for fixed components σ′ at R∖{q}, not for all Σ. It should also say that the theorems fail whenever Π ≅ Π ⊗ χ, including when K splits at q: then M_q is a scalar, the sign depends on σ′ alone, and a suitable singleton U′ already gives average 0 or 1. Otherwise the fix is right: kind 'error', affects 'a stated result', G-SO3 resolved, and both briefs and the report updated.

Item /48. §14.3 (p. 99) opens 'We retain the setting of §14.2, and assume that k is algebraically closed'. Theorem 14.5 and Lemma 14.6 (surjectivity of x ↦ ([x], [x_H])) are stated there; §14 otherwise has k of characteristic 0 only. The item drops the hypothesis. I checked the counterexample with the paper's own definitions (§13.4.1: in the odd orthogonal case ev(x) omits the obvious zero). For compact (SO(3), SO(2)), x ∈ so(3) ↔ v ∈ R³ gives [x] ↔ A = |v|² with ev(x) = {±i|v|}, and x_H is rotation by v₃, so [x_H] = v₃ and ev(x_H) = {±iv₃}. The real image is {(A, b) : A ⩾ b²}. A pair with b² > A (or A < 0) is stable (disjoint eigenvalues) but has no real preimage. So on real points the fibre O^{λ,µ} of (14.5) is empty, not an H-torsor, and g → [g] × [h] is not surjective. Nuance: read scheme-theoretically (fibres as R-varieties, possibly non-trivial torsors without real points), Theorem 14.5 descends to any field of characteristic 0. But the item, like (14.5), speaks of sets of elements x ∈ g, and on points it is false over R. The fix, prefixing 'over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0' and recording Theorem 17.1's 'empty or an H-torsor' over R, is right. Item /56. p. 117 reads 'if (λ_π, λ_σ) is stable and O_{π,σ} is non-empty, then … O_{π,σ} = O_π(λ_σ) = O^{λ_π,λ_σ} (17.3)'. The item keeps only 'when stable', so the statement is false as written. The red team's stated reason ('for SO(2,1) two real orbits share an infinitesimal character') does not hold. The non-identity component of SO(2,1) reverses time orientation and exchanges the two sheets, so SO(2,1) acts transitively on each regular real fibre; the example must use a group with genuinely split real fibres. A correct counterexample is (G, H) = (U(1,1), U(1)), with π a holomorphic discrete series whose orbit O_π is one elliptic orbit. For X = [[ia, b], [b̄, id]] with eigenvalues iα, iβ (α > β), one has |b|² = (a − α)(a − β), so the real fibre O^{λ_π} has two sheets, a ⩾ α and a ⩽ β, and these are distinct U(1,1)-orbits. Take µ = ia with a < β, which is stable. Then O^{λ_π,µ} is a non-empty U(1)-torsor (a circle in b), while O_π(µ) = O_{π,σ} = ∅. The added non-emptiness hypothesis is exactly what forces equality, since a non-empty H-invariant subset of an H-torsor is all of it. The fix for /56 ('when (λ_π, λ_σ) is stable and O_{π,σ} is non-empty') is right. The evidence should cite the U(1,1) ⊃ U(1) example instead of SO(2,1).

All four checked in the published text and arXiv v3 (identical in each). None is among E1–E15. (a) Lemma 8.10 (pp. 61–62) says Σ_j T_j 'converges in the Banach space of bounded linear operators', i.e. in norm. Counterexample: T_j = the orthogonal projection onto Ce_j. Then T_j*T_k = T_jT_k* = δ_{jk}T_j, so both Cotlar–Stein sums equal 1, but ‖S_n − S_m‖ = 1 for partial sums with n ≠ m, so the series is not norm-Cauchy. It converges strongly, which is what [Hör, Lemma 18.6.5] asserts. The only use (proof of Proposition 8.7, p. 62) needs just the norm bound and strong convergence. Kind error, affects nothing. (b) (8.3) (p. 57): ∂^α a_h^∨(x) ≪ h^{−dim g}|x/h^{1−δ}|^{−N}. Since a_h^∨(x) = h^{−n}a^∨(x/h), ∂^α a_h^∨(x) = h^{−n−|α|}(∂^α a^∨)(x/h). For fixed Schwartz a (in every S^m, δ = 0) and x = hu with ∂^α a^∨(u) ≠ 0, the left side is ≍ h^{−n−|α|} and the right side ≍ h^{−n}, so (8.3) fails. Integrating by parts, using ∂^α a^∨ = ((−ξ)^α a)^∨ and (∂^γ b)^∨ = x^γ b^∨, gives the corrected bound h^{−n−|α|}|x/h^{1−δ}|^{−N}. The only use (proof of Lemma 5.4, p. 57) is at |x| > ε, where h^{−|α|} is absorbed by taking N larger. Kind error, affects nothing. (c) §2.5 (p. 28): with Op_h(a, χ) := Op(a_h, χ) (2.2) and Lemma 2.1, Op_h(a)Op_h(b) = Op(a_h ⋆ b_h, χ′) = Op((a⋆_h b)_h, χ′) = Op_h(a⋆_h b, χ′). The printed Op is a misprint for Op_h, as in Theorem 5.8 (p. 40). The same slip recurs in the proof of Proposition 8.7 (p. 62), 'Op(a_{ω1})*Op(a_{ω2}) = Op(ā_{ω1} ⋆_h a_{ω2}, χ′)', and could be recorded with it. (d) Lemma 7.14 (p. 56). The Fourier convention is a^∨(x) = ∫a(ξ)e^{−xξ}dξ (§2.1), and (4.1) gives (∂^α a)^∨ = x^α a^∨ with ordinary Taylor expansion for ψ. Hence b_h^∨ = ψa_h^∨ ∼ Σ(∂^αψ(0)/α!)x^α a_h^∨ = Σ(∂^αψ(0)/α!)(∂^α(a_h))^∨, and ∂^α(a_h) = h^{|α|}(∂^α a)_h. So the coefficient is +h^j, not (−h)^j. The uses (§12.1, and §19.5 around (19.24)) keep only the leading term or the shape of the terms. Misprint, affects nothing. The fix (four item corrections and four new sourceIssues, 'also arXiv v3') is right.

Checked each item against the published text. /75: Definition 24.3(ii) on p. 159 reads 'there are φ, φ₊ ∈ H^J, with φ₊ positive definite and φ₊(1) ⩽ ε'; the item drops 'positive definite', so it defines a weaker notion of allowability. The finding's reason is overstated, though: (24.4) by itself already forces tr σ(φ₊) ≥ |k(σ) − tr σ(φ)| ≥ 0 for every σ in Ĥ, and (24.7) follows from the Plancherel formula for φ and φ₊ without positive-definiteness. The clause matters because it is part of the definition and is what Remark 24.4 ((24.6)) and Lemma 31.9 use ('a positive-definite element φ₊'). /68: (22.8) is a standing supposition stated just before Theorem 22.2 ('we suppose given an h-dependent family of maps H_σ that factors … with the first arrow h-uniformly continuous'), and the proof of (22.11) on p. 148 invokes it ('by the assumed uniform continuity of (22.8), we have H_σ(E) ≪ h^N'). The item mentions it only in the note and also drops the uniformity 'The implied constant may depend upon (N, k, a, ε), but not upon (π, σ, h)', which the global argument needs. /40: Lemma A.1(i) on p. 137 is for τ-isotypic v. The unrestricted statement is false. Take G = SL₂(R), K = SO(2), π an irreducible principal series (all K-types e^{inθ}, each once), and v = v₀ + δ·Σ_{0<|n|≤m} v_n with unit K-type vectors v_n. Then dim(Kv) = 2m+1, so dim(Kv)·‖v‖² ≥ 2m+1. But ‖κv‖² = κ₀² + δ²Σκ_n² → κ₀² as δ → 0. Choosing 2m+1 > κ₀² and then δ small violates the inequality. /50: Lemma 15.3 itself, the eigenvalue identity (15.3), needs no temperedness. The Γ_R product is derived on p. 107 only 'if π is a tempered representation of G … and similarly σ a tempered representation of H', and it fails in general for non-tempered parameters: for a character |x|^u of R^× with Re u < 0 the factor is Γ_R(s+u+ε), not Γ_R(s+u⁺+ε). §15.2 restricts to K = R (p. 105), and §15.1 takes G over R. /61–/62: §19 opens 'We assume that (G, H) is a GGP pair over an archimedean local field' and §19.1 takes π, σ tempered. The finding's 'Lemma 19.1(iii)' is a misreference: Lemma 19.1 has no part (iii) in the published text or in arXiv v3. The archimedean statement with a part (iii) is Lemma 18.1(iii), and /59 already states that one archimedeanly. The point is minor because Op_h and S_δ^{−∞} exist only archimedeanly, but the standing hypotheses should be explicit. /61 also omits 'π, σ tempered', which the finding does not mention. /99: the phrase 'For fixed Π and Σ whose … tend to ∞' can be misparsed as both being fixed. p. 4 says 'Π is fixed, while Σ traverses a sequence …'. This is a presentation point. Right fix. /75: add 'φ₊ positive definite'. /68: as proposed, (22.8) as a hypothesis plus the uniformity sentence. /40: 'for τ-isotypic v' (and F archimedean, π irreducible admissible). /50: attach 'π, σ tempered' to the Γ_R-product clause only, not to the eigenvalue identity, and add 'K = R'. /49 and /51: add 'over R'; /51 needs no temperedness. /61 and /62: add '(G, H) a GGP pair over an archimedean local field' (the standing assumption of §19, which covers Lemmas 19.1–19.2 and Theorem 19.3); also add 'π, σ tempered' to /61. /99: reword as proposed, preferably also saying 'under the assumptions of Theorem 31.11, for Σ in the families F_h'.

Checked, and the duplication is real. PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21 puts item /25 (Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula for connected reductive G over R, in the L2 form on the Schwartz algebra S(G)) and item /20(b) (every irreducible admissible representation is a Langlands quotient of a standard module) in its route 1. That route is a Part II of AutomorphicSpectralTheory, and its review accepts it (merged 23 September, after this paper's review). make_queue merges it into the pending DESIGN-AutomorphicSpectralTheoryPartII. Its brief schedules '(4) Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula', and its reason says that theorem 'is not planned anywhere and is only needed here'. This extraction takes /30 (§9.6, p. 75: real reductive G, [Kn, Thm 8.54]) and /64 (§A.3, p. 138) as missing items of route 1. The two Plancherel statements are one theorem. Nelson–Venkatesh's f(1) = ∫ χ_π(f) dπ on C_c^∞ follows from the L2 form by polarisation, since (f2* ∗ f1)(1) = ⟨f1, f2⟩ and every function in C_c^∞ is a sum of convolutions (Dixmier–Malliavin). The converse comes from applying it to f* ∗ f. No stage in data/atlas.json mentions Plancherel or the Langlands classification. The RT-AREA-automorphic-1/2 verdict ('choose one AF real-representation successor') and its merged fixes report create AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1b for the real Langlands classification. AF.1b is not yet in data/atlas.json, so it becomes a third owner only once the maintainer applies it. The red team wrote that fixes report, and says so. Its evidence here does not depend on that report. Confirmed. The fix needs three changes. (1) /30. The finding says to keep /30 missing but out of route 1. The paper checker then fails with 'missing but no route takes it'. 'Planned at AF.1b' also fails until AF.1b is a layer of the atlas. Instead, move /30 to a new source route to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups, stage AF.1, which now owns real reductive representation theory. Add a note that AF.1b takes it once the RT-AREA-automorphic-1 fixes are applied; their §7 retargets the AF.1 routes of CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 and GAN-ICHINO-18 in the same way. Route 1's brief then imports the classification. Tell the maintainer that BLZZ-21 /20(b) should import from AF.1b too. (2) The real half of /64. Choose AutomorphicSpectralTheory Part II as the owner. Its route was accepted with an explicit plan for this theorem, and its design comes first in the queue (order 63 against 151). Put the real Plancherel theorem on a part-ii route with parent AutomorphicSpectralTheory, using BLZZ-21's roadmap id and title so that make_queue merges it into that design. State it in the form this paper uses: f(1) = ∫ χ_π(f) for f in C_c^∞, and its extension to n-times differentiable compactly supported f, for every real reductive group, complex groups included by restriction of scalars. Route 1 imports it. /65, the extension to the space F of Lemma A.4, stays in route 1. (3) The p-adic half is not a duplicate. Nothing plans Waldspurger's Plancherel formula, and SR.3 does not either (see finding 6). Do not send it to SR.3 as an import.

Checked. Lemma 23.4 (p. 155) is Harish-Chandra's theorem, for any reductive H over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero (the opening of §23). Every tempered irreducible π is a subquotient of i_M σ, equivalently a submodule, for a unique class of pairs (M, σ) with σ square-integrable. The two agree because i_M σ is unitary, hence semisimple. PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 item rev-langlands-classification-and-harish-chandra (b) states the same result: π is a direct summand, and (M, δ) is unique up to conjugacy, for connected reductive G over a p-adic field. That item is on route 3, a source route to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3, accepted by the review merged on 23 September. PAPER-LIU-ETAL-22's item tempered-from-discrete-series is on its accepted route 12 to ET.4 and ET.7a. SR.3 plans the matrix-coefficient criteria for temperedness, which is where this theorem belongs. Route 1 would plan it a third time. Confirmed. The fix for /72 is right. A source route to SR.3 is the better of its two options, because SR.3's text does not name the theorem. The second half of the fix is wrong. SR.3 does not plan the p-adic Plancherel formula (Waldspurger's account of Harish-Chandra). SR.3 covers admissibility, finite length of induction, contragredients, the criteria for temperedness and supercuspidality, supercuspidal support and the Bernstein centre. I searched every item and brief: no stage or route plans p-adic Plancherel. Moving it 'with /72' would add a major theorem to SR.3 under the label of an import. Either keep the p-adic Plancherel formula in route 1, together with its direct corollary ∫ dim π^U < ∞ (§A.4.1). Or, better under §15, give both a part-ii route with parent SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups; make_queue merges it into DESIGN-SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroupsPartII, next to GAN-SAVIN-23-B's accepted unitary-dual proposal. Route 1 then imports them. For the lead: GAN-SAVIN-23 route 3 (SR.3) and LIU-ETAL-22 route 12 (ET.4/ET.7a) already duplicate each other on this theorem. ET should import it from SR.3.

Checked. Lemma 14.1 (p. 96) is background GIT for a reductive group acting on an affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. On p. 97, just before (14.2), the paper recalls the Hilbert–Mumford criterion in the form 'x is not H-stable iff some non-trivial cocharacter has only non-negative weights on x'. It uses this for H acting linearly on g (Theorem 14.2) and on m (Lemmas 19.7–19.8). PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 4 is an accepted Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups. It is pending as DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII, because ReductiveGroupsPartII already exists. That route plans orbit closures, affine semistability and closed orbits (/32) and Kempf's rational destabilising cocharacter (/32a). So the Hilbert–Mumford theorem would be planned twice. Confirmed. The fix is incomplete, and as written it creates a new duplicate. Two accepted source routes already send affine invariant theory to LanglandsParameterStacks LP2 and LP3. PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 route 2, item /4, sends the categorical quotient X⫽G = Spec k[X]^G. It is integral and affine, surjective on points over algebraically closed fields, has one closed orbit in each fibre and separates disjoint closed invariant sets (Seshadri). The same item has stability of tuples, meaning a closed orbit with finite stabiliser modulo the centre. PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 route 3, item /35, sends Richardson's closed-orbit theorem, which uses the Hilbert–Mumford theorem [Ric88, Thm 2.1]. The finding names neither route. Adding 'M//H affine with φ surjective and universal' to the Part III design would plan the categorical quotient a second time. The two forms of the theorem also differ. FINTZEN's /32a is the null-cone form (0 lies in the orbit closure). The paper needs the stability form. That form follows from the closed-orbit form of Hilbert–Mumford (Richardson, Kempf) together with Matsushima's theorem: a closed orbit has reductive stabiliser, and an infinite reductive stabiliser contains a non-trivial torus. Whoever owns the theorem must state this form. Right fix: route 1 imports affine GIT and never plans it. Route /46 on a part-ii route with parent tauceti ReductiveGroups, with the id and title of FINTZEN-21 route 4, so that make_queue merges it into DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII, the most foundational owner under §15. Ask that design for four things: the categorical quotient, openness of M^s and φ(M^s), the principal-bundle statement [MFK, Prop. 0.9], and the stability form of Hilbert–Mumford. Add a note for the maintainer. BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 route 2 and LAFFORGUE-18 route 3 plan the same quotient and Hilbert–Mumford theory at LP2/LP3, so one owner must be chosen and the other must import. That decision lies beyond this extraction. If the maintainer prefers LP2/LP3, mark the quotient and Hilbert–Mumford parts of /46 planned there, and route only the stable-locus and principal-bundle parts. Also correct /46's 'x is unstable iff …' to 'x is not H-stable iff …'. With 'unstable' in the usual null-cone sense the statement is false. Take G_m acting trivially on A^1 and x = 1: the identity cocharacter has only the weight 0 on x, yet 0 is not in the orbit closure.

Checked. (18.1) on p. 121 is the convergence ∫_H Ξ_G Ξ_H < ∞ of Ichino–Ikeda and N. Harris. The integrand of (18.2), ∫_H ⟨s v1, v2⟩⟨u, s u⟩ ds, is the unnormalised Ichino–Ikeda/Harris local period of π ⊠ σ̄ on the diagonal H ⊂ G × H. PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22 item /4 defines exactly this integral for unitary pairs, normalised by 𝓛(½, σ_v)^{-1}, with its absolute convergence (Harris, Prop. 2.1). The item is on route 4 to GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups, which the review accepts. This extraction splits the same object. It puts /59 in route 1, but sends positivity (/60), non-vanishing and ℓ_σ (/66), and the global H of /80 (∫_{H_R} ⟨h v1, v2⟩⟨u1, h u2⟩) to route 2. So the object is split between two new roadmaps, and its definition is planned twice. Confirmed. One change to the fix. Lemma 18.1(i) says more than (18.1). It says that the sum over an orthonormal basis B(σ) converges, that is, σ(f) is trace class for f(s) = ⟨s v1, v2⟩ (18.6). Its proof in §A.6 rests on §A.5, the Plancherel formula for Ξ-integrable functions (/65), which stays in route 1. So route 2 should get (18.1) and the local period for each pair of vectors. It should cover the orthogonal and general linear GGP pairs as well as the unitary ones that BCZ-22 covers. Checked. The proof of Theorem 27.7 (pp. 183–185) uses Ratner's measure classification [Rat] on Γ\G∞. Here G∞ = G0(R) is a real semisimple group once the centre is divided out, Γ is a cocompact arithmetic lattice, and U is the connected unipotent group generated by the exponentials of the centraliser of a regular nilpotent. The proof also uses the ergodic decomposition [EW, §8.7] and, in Lemma 27.8, Borel's density theorem [Mo, Prop. 4.7.1]. GN.4 only says 'separately schedule ergodic/mixing, unipotent-flow and nondivergence proofs needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications'. None of the 77 nodes of the GN packet concerns dynamics; the 15 at GN.4 are all lattice-point counting. The packet's coverage lists 'independent mixing/nondivergence/Oppenheim/Duke branches' as still to do. No stage in data/atlas.json mentions Ratner. The confirmed finding RT-AREA-iwasawa-1/1 reads GN.4 the same way for the S-arithmetic theorem. Ratner's classification in this generality is far more than the Oppenheim and Duke applications need; Margulis's proof of Oppenheim does not use it. The extraction itself hedged, and nothing else routes Ratner. Borel's density theorem has no item. Confirmed. Take the second of the two fixes, not the first. The merged RT-AREA-iwasawa-1 fixes (finding /1) make GN.4 the owner of unipotent-flow theorems. GN.4 keeps the real case, and a new suffix stage, GN.4:padic-unipotent-flows, takes Margulis–Tomanov and Ratner over Q_p. Their report adds that if a separate Ratner roadmap is preferred, it would take 'Ratner's theorems (real and S-arithmetic)' together. Routing the real theorem to the orbit-method roadmap would split Ratner theory between two owners. So add a requests entry to the GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic packet asking GN.4 to plan three things. First, Ratner's measure classification: for a connected real Lie group, a lattice and a subgroup generated by Ad-unipotent one-parameter subgroups, every ergodic invariant probability measure is the homogeneous measure on a closed orbit of a closed connected subgroup containing that subgroup. Second, ergodic decomposition for such actions; neither library has it in this form. Third, Borel's density theorem in the form cited: for a lattice Γ_S in a closed connected subgroup S, the real points of the Zariski closure of Γ_S contain every unipotent element of S. While that request is pending, a source route is better than 'planned'. Set /89 to missing and route it, with a new item for Borel's density theorem, on a source route to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, stage GN.4. Route 1's brief then imports from GN.4 ('Ratner's theorem from GN.4' can stay).

I checked each sub-item at its published locator and in arXiv v3. None is in E1–E15, and the review added none. (i) p. 136 integrates over ‖s − 1‖ ⩾ h^{1/2−η}, the region Lemma 19.8 (p. 133) makes O(h^∞); the next sentence ('write s = exp(y), pull back to the Lie algebra') needs ‖s − 1‖ ⩽ h^{1/2−η}. Confirmed, also in v3. (ii) p. 147: a is chosen with |k − ∫_{O(µ)}a²| ⩽ ε₁ on all of U, and a₂ with ∫_{O(µ)}a₂² ⩾ 2ε₁ only on U₀ (with closure(U₀) ⊆ image(V) ⊆ U). For hλ_σ ∈ U∖U₀, H_σ(Op_h(a)²) ≈ ∫a² can be as large as ε₁ while ∫a₂² may vanish, so (22.10) is unproved there. Confirmed, also in v3. The repair needs more than stated: a must also be chosen with the image of its support compact in U₀ (or a₂ large on that image). Then (22.10) holds up to an additive O(h^N), which the sums in Lemma 30.6 absorb via the weak Weyl law (29.2). Since the exact inequality cannot be expected where both sides are O(h^∞), the stated Theorem 22.2(iii) itself should carry the +O(h^N). I would record affects 'a stated result (Theorem 22.2(iii)); the main theorems are unaffected' rather than 'the proof'. (iii) Example 24.7 (p. 165). For η unramified quadratic, η∘det (α = −q^{−1/2}), St ⊗ η∘det and the twisted complementary series π(η|·|^s, η|·|^{−s}), 0 < s < ½, are unitary with trivial central character and lie in the unramified principal-series component. So Θ^unit ≅ C^(1) ∪ ([q^{−1/2}, q^{1/2}] ∪ [−q^{1/2}, −q^{−1/2}])/∼. For odd n, f(−t) = −f(t), so f ⩾ 1 fails on the negative part of Θ^nt. The printed Θ^nt also omits the endpoint q^{±1/2}, which lies in Θ^unit ∖ Θ⁰ by definition. Lemma 24.10 itself survives, since the closure of Θ^nt still meets Θ⁰ in a null set. The E3 amendment is right. I would record (iii) as that amendment to E3, kind error, rather than as a separate new 'misprint'. Also in v3. (iv) p. 185: the proof must show s ⊇ g ('We must show that s contains g'); 'This implies s⩽g' is reversed. Also in v3. (v) p. 4 says |F_h| ≈ C⁴, but Lemma 31.10 (p. 202) gives C ≍ |F_h|⁴, which is what the o(C^{1/4}) bound (1.4) needs. Also in v3. (vi) p. 136: κ = −cΣx² acts by 0 on the trivial K-type, contradicting (ii), (iii) and Lemma A.1(ii) (π(κ) invertible). Moreover, even 1 − cΣx² fails (ii) and (iii) once K has rank ⩾ 2 (for SO(4), dim τ grows like |λ|² and Σκ_τ^{−1} diverges). The correct explicit choice is a power (1 − Σx²)^N with N large in terms of K, or the parenthesis should be dropped. This is an error rather than a misprint, affecting nothing. Also in v3. (vii) pp. 110–111: the fibre of g*×h* → [g*]×[h*] is O^λ × O^µ, of dimension 2 dim H; the map meant is ξ ↦ ([ξ], [ξ|_h]) on g*, as in the bottom row of (16.4). Also in v3. (viii) The page image of p. 95 shows both lines of the centralizer list ending x^{dim(U)−2}, with no y, while y is defined below. The v3 text and source have ', y' in the dim(U′) = 1 line. Published text only; confirmed. (ix) p. 134: 'ψ ≡ 1 on B(ω, 2h^δ) and ψ ≡ 0 on B(ω, 3h^δ)' is self-contradictory; 'outside' is meant. Also in v3. (x) p. 79: the h² coefficient of q ⋆_h Σh^j b_j is qb₂ + q⋆₁b₁ + q⋆₂b₀, so b₂ = −(q⋆₂b₀ + q⋆₁b₁)/q; the printed sign of q⋆₁b₁ is wrong. Also in v3. (xi) p. 69: for b ≡ q ⋆_h Z with Z = z^{s+2k}, one needs q₁ = −(q₀⋆₁Z)/Z. Since ⋆₁ is a multiple of the Poisson bracket, b⋆₁q₀ = −q₀(q₀⋆₁Z), so the printed q₁ is wrong. The printed q₂ = (−b⋆₂q₀ + b⋆₁q₁)/Z is wrong too; it should be −(q₀⋆₂Z + q₁⋆₁Z)/Z, and in general q_j = −(Σ_{l<j} q_l ⋆_{j−l} Z)/Z. The correction should cover the whole recursion. Also in v3. (xii) p. 43: 'd the maximal dimension of any coadjoint orbit, so that … every orbit in O_π is 2d-dimensional' is inconsistent; d is half that dimension (as §26.4 says). Also in v3. (xiii) p. 88 (12.3): '(O, π)' for (O, ω). The same slip recurs on p. 176 (§26.4, 'regular limit coadjoint orbit (O, π)'), which should be added. Both in v3. (xiv) p. 191: Cauchy–Schwarz gives |tr(T₁T₂)|² ⩽ tr(T₁*T₁)tr(T₂*T₂), and the next sentence uses tr(T₁*T₁) ≪ h^∞. Also in v3. (xv) The bibliography's [Z1] is Zhang, Ann. of Math. 180 (2014). I opened the author's copy: its Theorem 1.1 assumes '(1) Every archimedean place is split in E/F' and two split supercuspidal places, and proves the equivalence L(½) ≠ 0 ⟺ distinction. Its introduction says 'A subsequent paper [63] is devoted to the refined conjecture for unitary groups', and Remark 7 says the same. The refined formula (1.1) is Zhang's JAMS 27 (2014) paper, which is not cited. So pp. 3 and 204 and the /81 note misattribute; v3 cites the same Annals paper (labelled [Z2] there). The '(U2, U1) only' remark also holds. Split archimedean places make G_p = GL_{n+1}, so §25.7(3) forces a single archimedean place. A hermitian space of dimension ⩾ 3 whose archimedean places split is isotropic (trace form of dimension ⩾ 6 at finite places, hyperbolic at split places, then Hasse–Minkowski). So anisotropy forces dim V = 2. (xvi) Lemma 23.4 is on p. 155, not p. 154. The G-for-H slips recur in §23.1 (p. 152: 'i^G_M = Ind^G_P … to smooth representations of G', 'subquotients of i^G_M τ') and in the proof of Lemma 23.2 (pp. 153–154: 'an element of g', 'π ↪ i^G_M(wτ)', 'π → i^G_P τ'). Fix: apply it with the refinements above. (ii): stated result Theorem 22.2(iii), with the support condition on a in the repair. (iii): as the E3 amendment. (vi): error, with κ = (1 − Σx²)^N. (xi): the whole recursion. (xiii): add p. 176. The rest as proposed.
